correctness.rationale: The one-agent EF1 events are independent across the two agents. Two goods split one per agent satisfy EF1 surely. For three goods expected fairness forces probabilities (x+y,x,y); comparison of all singleton partitions gives exact nonnegative gaps y² and x², while an empty-bundle assignment cannot beat the fair singleton split. The four-good exact probability formulas and their difference have been verified with rational enumeration of all 256 joint binary realizations. The cubic factor is strictly decreasing on the stated domain, establishing its unique zero and the open counterexample range. The example has only one ex-ante EF partition up to exchange.

value.rationale: The first possible failure of optimizing ex-post EF1 by expected-envy-free assignment is a natural structural boundary in stochastic fair division, motivated by a recent paper that explicitly raises EF1. It holds with fully bounded, independent, individually log-concave binary values and common per-good laws across agents; the small strict gain is only a witness, while the sharp domain threshold and interval establish the substantive limitation of expectation-based allocation.
